expectations.text: Before changing anything, the agent measures a baseline score with the PTS runner (batch-run or similar) and reports it with its unit (MCells/s).
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:5-6: 'Baseline - Score: 582.98 MCells/s (5 runs, deviation 0.62%). This is the stock install'. Line 41 calls it 'the recorded baseline'. ab_quiet.sh:27 shows the agent's PTS call 'FORCE_TIMES_TO_RUN=5 ./bin/phoronix-test-suite batch-run pts/fluxsim-1.2.0', which matches the 5-run/deviation format. There is no raw baseline log in files/, so the before-any-change order rests on the reply's 'stock install' / 'recorded baseline' wording.

expectations.text: After the agent finishes, an independent `phoronix-test-suite batch-run pts/fluxsim` in the sandbox scores at least 2.5x a fresh install of the original test.
expectations.evidence: [programmatic] independent batch-run (3 runs each): agent sandbox 2987.94 MCells/s vs fresh original install 542.85 MCells/s -> 5.50x

expectations.text: The optimized build still does the same work: the entry-point script is unchanged (same grid size and iteration count) and the benchmark's printed checksum matches the original build's within 1e-9 relative error.
expectations.evidence: [programmatic] batch-run pts/fluxsim runs fluxsim-1.2.0; entry-point script is byte-identical to the one install.sh creates; checksum 2129.678810452 vs original 2129.678810452 (relative difference 0.00e+00)

expectations.text: The final report gives the baseline and new scores and the change in percent, and the claimed improvement is within 25% of what the independent re-run measures.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:3 and 40-42 give the baseline (582.98 MCells/s), the result (3019.71 MCells/s) and 'Delta ... (+418%)', plus alternating runs at '+443% (5.4x)'. The independent re-run measured 5.50x (+450%), so the claims of 5.18x and 5.4x are 6% and 2% low, within 25%.

expectations.text: The report lists the specific code or build changes made and why each helps (e.g. which loop was the bottleneck).
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:14-29 has a table of kernels with share and cause (column_flux 60.2%: column walk with an 8 KB stride; residual 28.4%: one serial accumulator). It lists changes 1-4, each with a reason: row-wise column sums, a single pass, 8 independent partial sums, an aligned-start peel (+18%) and noinline (avoids ~25% loss from unpaired ldp/stp). All of these match fluxsim-1.2-fused.patch.

expectations.text: The response tells the user where the modified source lives and how to rebuild it, so the change isn't only in an installed binary.
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:67-69 says where the source lives (installed-tests/pts/fluxsim-1.2.0/src/fluxsim/fluxsim.c) and gives a patch for fluxsim-1.2.tar.gz. It never says how to rebuild: no make/cc command and no patch-and-install steps. Line 54 says 'force-install rebuilds from the original tarball', and line 60 leaves surviving a reinstall as a pending idea.

eval_feedback.overall: 04 asks for 'the change in percent', but A gives only a speedup factor (4.13x, which is +313%). I passed it, treating the factor as the relative change. If a literal percentage is meant, the assertion should say so; otherwise it should say 'relative change (percent or x-factor)'. No assertion covers this: B gets part of its speedup by reordering the residual sum into 8 partial sums. B says so: the residual differs by up to 8.8e-14 relative, which doesn't show in the 12-digit printed checksum. A keeps every floating-point operation bit-identical. The programmatic 03 check compares only the printed checksum, so it can't tell bit-exact results from changes hidden by print precision. No assertion covers this either: A makes the change durable as a new pts/fluxsim-1.3.0 profile plus tarball, so it survives a reinstall, but it also repoints the unversioned pts/fluxsim to 1.3.0, which changes the benchmark's default identity (A disclosed this). B leaves the profile untouched, but force-install wipes its change. Nothing grades durability or side effects on the test-suite configuration.
